trigger: A change adds, removes, replaces, updates, pins, vendors, generates, downloads, or changes the resolution or execution of a third-party dependency, package manager, registry, lockfile, build plugin, action, container base, or fetched build artifact.
exitSignal: Each changed third-party component is necessary, resolves reproducibly from an approved provenance, has current advisory and license assessment, has reviewed transitive and build-script impact, and passes focused compatibility plus repository verification with residual risk disclosed.
evidence: A dependency delta identifies direct and transitive additions, removals, versions, sources, integrity data, lockfile changes, scripts or plugins, and runtime or build-time placement.
A necessity record explains why platform, standard-library, or current dependency capabilities cannot meet the accepted outcome.
Provenance evidence identifies configured source, available publisher or owner, integrity mechanism, release identity, and vendored or generated origin.

Current advisory and maintenance evidence records the approved source, source identity, result time or advisory-database identity, severity disposition, supported versions, and signs of abandonment or compromise; evidence becomes stale after advisory-database changes unless its identity still matches.
License evidence identifies declared licenses and compatibility with project policy, escalating ambiguity instead of guessing.
Focused tests cover changed behavior, and clean or frozen restore evidence proves reproducibility and detects unexpected artifacts or scripts where supported.
High-risk updates include release-guidance review, transitive diff, rollback, and residual-risk disclosure without automatic network, install, update, or publication actions.
